428	## 7. Risques et pièges
429	
430	1. **Vrai signal en test.** Trois verrous : (a) `realOS.kill` panique dans un binaire de test sans `allowRealSignals(t)` ; (b) `newTestModel` remplace `ops` dans netdiag, donc même une `Cmd` exécutée n'atteint pas `ports.Kill` ; (c) `seedNetdiagFooter` (`internal/app`) n'exécute pas ses `Cmd` et vise un PID au-dessus de `pid_max`. Le seul vrai signal vise un enfant lancé par le test, attendu en `t.Cleanup`. Ne jamais appeler `allowRealSignals` dans un test qui vise autre chose que son propre enfant.
431	2. **Rule 110.** La cible est copiée dans `confirmKill` (Update) ; `handleConfirmYes` (Update) lit `pendingKill` et passe à `killProcessCmd` des valeurs (`kill`, `pid`) ; la `Cmd` ne lit jamais le modèle. Les seams de `ports` ne sont écrits que par les tests de `ports`, jamais pendant qu'une `Cmd` tourne ; `realSignalsAllowed` est un `atomic.Bool`. `mise run test-race` obligatoire.
432	3. **Rafraîchissement 2 s pendant la confirmation.** Volontairement conservé (option C rejetée) : `handleData` → `SetItems` peut déplacer le curseur, et c'est sans effet puisque `Yes` ne lit plus la sélection. Ne pas « corriger » en mettant le tick en pause. `Yes` arrive par une `Cmd` : un `portsDataMsg` peut s'intercaler entre `enter` et `Yes` ; le test 714 le reproduit.
433	4. **PID réutilisé pendant une confirmation longue.** La capture élargit la fenêtre : si la modale reste ouverte longtemps, que le processus sort et que son PID est repris, `Yes` signale le nouveau venu. S-01b (identité à chaque signal) ferme ce cas ; d'ici là, voir **Q1** (contrôle de présence dans le dernier tableau).
434	5. **WSL2.** `runtime.GOOS == "linux"` : la règle Windows ne s'applique pas ; PID 1 est `/init` de la VM, protégé ; le parent est le shell de la VM. Les processus de l'hôte Windows ne sont pas visibles (non-objectif). Hypothèse de la story confirmée par construction ; à vérifier à la main si une machine WSL2 est disponible.
435	6. **Espaces de noms PID et conteneurs.** `os.Getppid()` peut rendre 0 (parent hors de l'espace de noms) : règle du parent ignorée. DevDesk PID 1 dans un conteneur : raison `This is DevDesk itself`.
436	7. **Parent mort, sous-moissonneur.** Après la mort du parent, `getppid` rend PID 1 ou un sous-moissonneur (`systemd --user`, etc.), généralement né avant DevDesk : il sera grisé « This process started DevDesk ». Protection excessive, sans danger ; à documenter.
437	8. **Windows.** `os.Getppid` lit un instantané Toolhelp32 : le PID parent peut être celui d'un parent mort et repris ; la comparaison des heures règle ce cas. `CreateTime` du parent passe par `OpenProcess` : refusé (parent élevé) → protégé par prudence. PID 0 : `List` le vide déjà (`toSocket`), donc en pratique la ligne est grisée avec `reasonNoPID` ; la raison Windows ne s'affiche que pour une ligne `PID: "0"`, impossible aujourd'hui (voir Hypothèses).
438	9. **Coût par rendu.** `killable()` est appelé à chaque image de l'en-tête. Lecture d'heure seulement quand la ligne sélectionnée porte le PID du parent ; sous Windows, un `OpenProcess` par rendu sur cette ligne. Acceptable ; si une mesure le contredit, mémoriser le verdict par PID parent dans netdiag (pas dans ce lot).
439	10. **`testing` importé par du code de production.** Précédent : `internal/credentials/hoststore.go`. `testing.Testing()` est faux dans `dk`.
440	11. **Gardes existants.** `TestNothingHereRunsASubprocessOrTalksToDocker` ne lit que les fichiers non-test : l'`os/exec` du test d'intégration est permis. Le garde d'activité (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`) lit `ports_model.go` : pas de glyphe littéral, pas de nouveau fichier de vue à déclarer (`ports_commands.go` reste hors du garde).
441	12. **Irréversible.** Rien : aucun format de fichier, aucune configuration, aucune API externe ne change. Un revert rend le comportement actuel.

443	## 8. Questions bloquantes
444	
445	**Q1 — `Yes` alors que la cible n'est plus dans le tableau rafraîchi.** Le critère 6 dit que la confirmation reste sur sa cible si le processus disparaît du tableau, et que `No`/`esc` la ferme sans signal ; il ne dit pas ce que fait `Yes` dans ce cas. Le critère 5 dit seulement que `Yes` agit sur le PID capturé.
446	- (a) Signaler quand même le PID capturé (lecture littérale du critère 5). Si le processus est sorti : `PID N is no longer running` sous Unix. Si son PID a été repris pendant que la modale était ouverte : le nouveau processus est tué. S-01b fermera ce cas.
447	- (b) **Recommandé** : avant le signal, vérifier que le dernier tableau reçu contient encore une ligne avec ce PID **et** le même nom ; sinon aucun signal, pied de page Warn `node (PID 4242) is no longer listed — not stopped`. Coût nul (aucune lecture système), ferme l'essentiel de la fenêtre du risque 4 jusqu'à S-01b. Si le processus a seulement fermé son socket, le port est libéré : refuser ne contrarie pas le but de l'utilisateur. Limites : tableau en pause ou périmé → on se fie aux dernières données ; même nom après reprise du PID → non détecté (c'est S-01b).
448	- (c) Fermer la confirmation automatiquement dès que la cible disparaît du tableau. Contredit le critère 6 (« la confirmation reste sur sa cible »).

13	// What the package asks of the host about processes goes through these seams,
14	// so a test can substitute them (DEVDESK-708). They are written only by tests
15	// of this package, never while a Cmd runs.
16	var (
17		selfPID           = os.Getpid
18		parentPID         = os.Getppid
19		goos              = runtime.GOOS
20		procOS    osProcs = realOS{}
21	)
22	
23	// osProcs is everything this package asks the operating system about a single
24	// process: when it was created, and to end it.
25	type osProcs interface {
26		// createTime is the creation time in ms since the epoch. It is opaque: it
27		// is only compared with another value of the same function.
28		createTime(pid int) (int64, error)
29		// kill is SIGKILL, or TerminateProcess on Windows.
30		kill(pid int) error
31	}
32	
33	// realOS is the production osProcs.
34	type realOS struct{}
35	
36	func (realOS) createTime(pid int) (int64, error) {
37		p, err := gproc.NewProcess(int32(pid)) //nolint:gosec // a PID fits in int32 on every supported OS
38		if err != nil {
39			return 0, err
40		}
41		return p.CreateTime()
42	}
43	
44	// kill is the only place of this package that signals a process, and its first
45	// statement is the run-time guard (TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal).
46	func (realOS) kill(pid int) error {
47		refuseRealSignalUnderTest(pid)
48		p, err := os.FindProcess(pid)
49		if err != nil {
50			return fmt.Errorf("finding the process: %w", err)
51		}
52		return p.Kill()
53	}
54	
55	// realSignalsAllowed is flipped only by allowRealSignals(t) in the _test.go
56	// files of this package.
57	var realSignalsAllowed atomic.Bool
58	
59	// refuseRealSignalUnderTest panics in a test binary that did not allow real
60	// signals. It panics rather than returning an error: an error would be shown as
61	// an ordinary failed kill and the test could pass, leaving the guard silent.
62	func refuseRealSignalUnderTest(pid int) {
63		if testing.Testing() && !realSignalsAllowed.Load() {
64			panic(fmt.Sprintf("ports: a test reached a real signal to PID %d without a substituted procOS; "+
65				"replace procOS, or call allowRealSignals(t) for a child the test started "+
66				"(DEVDESK-708, docs/architecture/network.md)", pid))
67		}
68	}

2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strconv"
6	)
7	
8	// Protection says why DevDesk refuses to signal a process, or that it does not
9	// (DEVDESK-708). The zero value is Unprotected, so a Protection nobody set
10	// never blocks anything.
11	type Protection int
12	
13	const (
14		// Unprotected is a process DevDesk may signal.
15		Unprotected Protection = iota
16		// ProtectedSelf is DevDesk's own process.
17		ProtectedSelf
18		// ProtectedInit is PID 1.
19		ProtectedInit
20		// ProtectedWindowsSystem is PID 0 or 4 on Windows (Idle and System).
21		ProtectedWindowsSystem
22		// ProtectedParent is the process that started DevDesk: the direct parent
23		// only, never a grandparent.
24		ProtectedParent
25	)
26	
27	// The sentences shown to the user for each refusal.
28	const (
29		ReasonSelf          = "This is DevDesk itself"
30		ReasonParent        = "This process started DevDesk"
31		ReasonInit          = "PID 1 is the system's init process"
32		ReasonWindowsSystem = "Windows system process"
33	)
34	
35	// Reason is the sentence to show for p, or "" for Unprotected.
36	func (p Protection) Reason() string {
37		switch p {
38		case ProtectedSelf:
39			return ReasonSelf
40		case ProtectedParent:
41			return ReasonParent
42		case ProtectedInit:
43			return ReasonInit
44		case ProtectedWindowsSystem:
45			return ReasonWindowsSystem
46		default:
47			return ""
48		}
49	}
50	
51	// hostView is what protectionFor needs to know about the host. parentBornFirst
52	// is a function so the creation time, which costs a system call, is read only
53	// when the PID asked about is the parent's.
54	type hostView struct {
55		self, parent    int
56		windows         bool
57		parentBornFirst func() bool
58	}
59	
60	// protectionFor is the rule, free of any system call. The order matters when
61	// one PID qualifies twice: DevDesk itself first, then PID 1 (also a parent
62	// inside a container), then the Windows system PIDs, then the parent. A parent
63	// PID of 0 means unknown (the parent lives outside this PID namespace) and
64	// never matches.
65	func protectionFor(pid int, h hostView) Protection {
66		switch {
67		case pid == h.self:
68			return ProtectedSelf
69		case pid == 1:
70			return ProtectedInit
71		case h.windows && (pid == 0 || pid == 4):
72			return ProtectedWindowsSystem
73		case h.parent > 0 && pid == h.parent && h.parentBornFirst():
74			return ProtectedParent
75		default:
76			return Unprotected
77		}
78	}
79	
80	// parentStartedFirst reports whether parent was created no later than self. A
81	// parent born after DevDesk is a process that reused the PID of the real one,
82	// which exited. Anything unreadable, and a tie, counts as true: when in doubt
83	// the parent is protected.
84	func parentStartedFirst(parent, self int) bool {
85		parentCreated, err := procOS.createTime(parent)
86		if err != nil {
87			return true
88		}
89		selfCreated, err := procOS.createTime(self)
90		if err != nil {
91			return true
92		}
93		return parentCreated <= selfCreated
94	}
95	
96	// protectionOf feeds protectionFor from the seams.
97	func protectionOf(n int) Protection {
98		self, parent := selfPID(), parentPID()
99		return protectionFor(n, hostView{
100			self:            self,
101			parent:          parent,
102			windows:         goos == "windows",
103			parentBornFirst: func() bool { return parentStartedFirst(parent, self) },
104		})
105	}
106	
107	// parsePID reads a PID in the one form DevDesk accepts: canonical decimal that
108	// fits in 32 bits. The kernel keeps only 32 bits (pid_t on Unix, a DWORD on
109	// Windows), so a wider number would reach a different process than the one
110	// checked: "4294967295" would become kill(-1), "4294967297" PID 1. Kill is the
111	// exported border, so it is checked here, once, for Kill and ProtectionOf.
112	// Signs, leading zeros and spaces are refused: the text must be what
113	// strconv.Itoa prints.
114	func parsePID(pid string) (int, bool) {
115		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(pid, 10, 32)
116		if err != nil || strconv.Itoa(int(n)) != pid {
117			return 0, false
118		}
119		return int(n), true
120	}
121	
122	// ProtectionOf says whether DevDesk refuses to signal the process pid. An
123	// empty, non-numeric, out-of-range or non-canonical pid is Unprotected: Kill
124	// refuses it as not a process id, so there is nothing to protect. It runs on
125	// every render, hence the lazy creation-time read.
126	func ProtectionOf(pid string) Protection {
127		n, ok := parsePID(pid)
128		if !ok {
129			return Unprotected
130		}

1	// Package ports reads the machine's socket table, and ends a process holding
2	// one.
3	//
4	// It answers for **this machine**. That is the whole reason it exists: the
5	// Ports tab used to run `ss` inside `docker run --rm --net=host --pid=host
6	// --privileged`, and on Docker Desktop `--net=host` is the namespace of the
7	// Linux VM, not of the host. The tab therefore listed the VM's sockets — its
8	// NFS daemons, with two-digit PIDs — while not one of the host's listening
9	// sockets appeared, and `K` killed a process of the VM under the impression it
10	// was freeing a port on the machine (D55).
11	//
12	// The same sentence has been written at the top of `docker.runDiagHost` since
13	// §3.33 rapatriated DNS, ICMP, TCP, TLS and HTTP for exactly this reason.
14	// `RunSS` and `KillProcess` were the two that stayed behind.
15	//
16	// Nothing here starts a container, and nothing here needs Docker: the Ports tab
17	// now works on a machine that has none.
18	package ports
19	
20	import (
21		"context"
22		"fmt"
23		"net"
24		"strconv"
25	
26		gnet "github.com/shirou/gopsutil/v4/net"
27		gproc "github.com/shirou/gopsutil/v4/process"
28	)
29	
30	// Socket is one row of the table: a socket, and the process holding it.
31	//
32	// Every field is a string because every one of them is displayed, and the PID
33	// in particular is what the table is keyed on — an int would have to be
34	// formatted at each of the sites that compare it.
35	type Socket struct {
36		Protocol  string // tcp or udp, whichever family the address is on
37		State     string // LISTEN, ESTABLISHED, UNCONN, TIME_WAIT…
38		LocalAddr string
39		PeerAddr  string
40		PID       string // empty when no process could be attributed
41		Process   string
42	}
43	
44	// List returns the machine's TCP and UDP sockets.
45	//
46	// resolve asks for the addresses to be reported as host names where reverse DNS
47	// answers; see resolveAddrs for what that does and does not cover.
48	func List(ctx context.Context, resolve bool) ([]Socket, error) {
49		conns, err := gnet.ConnectionsWithContext(ctx, "inet")
50		if err != nil {
51			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading the socket table: %w", err)
52		}
53	
54		names := processNames(ctx)
55	
56		sockets := make([]Socket, 0, len(conns))
57		for _, c := range conns {
58			sockets = append(sockets, toSocket(c, names))
59		}
60	
61		if resolve {
62			resolveAddrs(ctx, sockets)
63		}
64		return sockets, nil
65	}
66	
67	// toSocket turns one connection into a row.
68	func toSocket(c gnet.ConnectionStat, names map[int32]string) Socket {
69		s := Socket{
70			Protocol:  protocolOf(c.Type),
71			State:     stateOf(c.Status, c.Type),
72			LocalAddr: formatAddr(c.Laddr, c.Family),
73			PeerAddr:  formatAddr(c.Raddr, c.Family),
74		}
75		// A PID of zero is not a process: it is the system declining to attribute
76		// the socket to one, and `K` keys on this field. Left as "0" it would give
77		// the row something that looks killable, and Kill would then be asked to
78		// signal a process id that means "every process in the group" on Unix.
79		if c.Pid > 0 {
80			s.PID = strconv.FormatInt(int64(c.Pid), 10)
81			s.Process = names[c.Pid]
82		}
83		return s
84	}
85	
86	// Kill sends SIGKILL — TerminateProcess on Windows — to the process holding a
87	// socket.
88	//
89	// It replaces `docker run --pid=host --privileged <image> kill -9 <pid>`, which
90	// on Docker Desktop signalled a process of the VM (D55). The consequence worth
91	// knowing is that DevDesk now signals with the rights it actually has: another
92	// user's process, or a service, comes back as a refusal from the operating
93	// system rather than as a success against the wrong machine.
94	//
95	// The signal leaves through procOS.kill, the single point of the package that
96	// sends one; in a test binary it panics unless the test substituted procOS
97	// (DEVDESK-708).
98	//
99	// DevDesk itself, its direct parent, PID 1 and, on Windows, PIDs 0 and 4 are
100	// refused with a *ProtectedError before anything is sent. A pid outside int32
101	// or not in canonical form is refused first, as "not a process id" (parsePID).
102	// The protection check comes
103	// before the n <= 0 one because PID 0 is a protected process on Windows.
104	func Kill(pid string) error {
105		n, ok := parsePID(pid)
106		if !ok {
107			return fmt.Errorf("not a process id: %q", pid)
108		}
109		if p := protectionOf(n); p != Unprotected {
110			return &ProtectedError{PID: n, Protection: p}
111		}
112		if n <= 0 {
113			return fmt.Errorf("not a process id: %q", pid)
114		}
115		if err := procOS.kill(n); err != nil {
116			return fmt.Errorf("killing process %s: %w", pid, err)
117		}
118		return nil
119	}
120	
121	// processNames maps PID to process name, from **one** enumeration.
122	//
123	// The obvious implementation — process.NewProcess(pid).Name() per socket — is
124	// the one that does not work. On Windows that path goes through OpenProcess and
125	// QueryFullProcessImageName, which needs rights over the target: measured on
126	// this machine, 98 of 189 sockets came back "Access denied", and the Process
127	// column would have been empty for every service on the box. Processes() reads
128	// a Toolhelp32 snapshot instead and named all 294 processes in 11 ms, elevated
129	// or not.
130	//
131	// So the bulk enumeration is not an optimisation over the per-PID call. It is
132	// the difference between a column that is filled in and one that is not.
133	//
134	// A failure here is not a failure of the listing: a table of sockets with no
135	// process names still says which ports are open, and that is most of what it is
136	// read for.
137	func processNames(ctx context.Context) map[int32]string {
138		procs, err := gproc.ProcessesWithContext(ctx)
139		if err != nil {
140			return nil
141		}
142		names := make(map[int32]string, len(procs))
143		for _, p := range procs {
144			if name, err := p.NameWithContext(ctx); err == nil && name != "" {
145				names[p.Pid] = name
146			}
147		}
148		return names
149	}
150	
151	// protocolOf reports tcp or udp. Both families print the same word, as `ss`
152	// does: the address beside it already says which one it is on.
153	func protocolOf(sockType uint32) string {
154		switch sockType {
155		case 1: // SOCK_STREAM
156			return "tcp"
157		case 2: // SOCK_DGRAM
158			return "udp"
159		default:
160			return ""
161		}
162	}
163	
164	// stateOf normalises the state, and neither substitution is cosmetic.
165	//
166	// An unconnected UDP socket is reported as "NONE" on Linux and as nothing at all
167	// on Windows, so the same socket read differently depending on where DevDesk was
168	// running. UNCONN is what the table showed when `ss` produced it, and it is what
169	// the socket is.
170	//
171	// ESTABLISHED is shortened to ESTAB for the reason `ss` shortens it: the State
172	// column is ten cells wide, so the long spelling is truncated to "ESTABLISHE" —
173	// and the filter token the user toggles with `e` reads better short.
174	func stateOf(status string, sockType uint32) string {
175		if sockType == 2 && (status == "" || status == "NONE") {
176			return "UNCONN"
177		}
178		if status == "ESTABLISHED" {
179			return "ESTAB"
180		}
181		return status
182	}
183	
184	// formatAddr renders an endpoint the way the table has always shown one:
185	// host:port, bracketed for IPv6, and the wildcard form for the peer of a socket
186	// that has none.
187	func formatAddr(a gnet.Addr, family uint32) string {
188		if a.IP == "" && a.Port == 0 {
189			if isIPv6(family) {
190				return "[::]:*"
191			}
192			return "0.0.0.0:*"
193		}
194		return net.JoinHostPort(a.IP, strconv.FormatUint(uint64(a.Port), 10))
195	}
196	
197	// isIPv6 reports whether the address family is AF_INET6. The constant differs
198	// between platforms — 23 on Windows, 10 on Linux, 30 on Darwin — and gopsutil
199	// passes through whichever the kernel used, so all three are named here rather
200	// than compared against one.
201	func isIPv6(family uint32) bool {
202		return family == 23 || family == 10 || family == 30
203	}

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function

    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**

428	## 7. Risques et pièges
429	
430	1. **Vrai signal en test.** Trois verrous : (a) `realOS.kill` panique dans un binaire de test sans `allowRealSignals(t)` ; (b) `newTestModel` remplace `ops` dans netdiag, donc même une `Cmd` exécutée n'atteint pas `ports.Kill` ; (c) `seedNetdiagFooter` (`internal/app`) n'exécute pas ses `Cmd` et vise un PID au-dessus de `pid_max`. Le seul vrai signal vise un enfant lancé par le test, attendu en `t.Cleanup`. Ne jamais appeler `allowRealSignals` dans un test qui vise autre chose que son propre enfant.
431	2. **Rule 110.** La cible est copiée dans `confirmKill` (Update) ; `handleConfirmYes` (Update) lit `pendingKill` et passe à `killProcessCmd` des valeurs (`kill`, `pid`) ; la `Cmd` ne lit jamais le modèle. Les seams de `ports` ne sont écrits que par les tests de `ports`, jamais pendant qu'une `Cmd` tourne ; `realSignalsAllowed` est un `atomic.Bool`. `mise run test-race` obligatoire.
432	3. **Rafraîchissement 2 s pendant la confirmation.** Volontairement conservé (option C rejetée) : `handleData` → `SetItems` peut déplacer le curseur, et c'est sans effet puisque `Yes` ne lit plus la sélection. Ne pas « corriger » en mettant le tick en pause. `Yes` arrive par une `Cmd` : un `portsDataMsg` peut s'intercaler entre `enter` et `Yes` ; le test 714 le reproduit.
433	4. **PID réutilisé pendant une confirmation longue.** La capture élargit la fenêtre : si la modale reste ouverte longtemps, que le processus sort et que son PID est repris, `Yes` signale le nouveau venu. S-01b (identité à chaque signal) ferme ce cas ; d'ici là, voir **Q1** (contrôle de présence dans le dernier tableau).
434	5. **WSL2.** `runtime.GOOS == "linux"` : la règle Windows ne s'applique pas ; PID 1 est `/init` de la VM, protégé ; le parent est le shell de la VM. Les processus de l'hôte Windows ne sont pas visibles (non-objectif). Hypothèse de la story confirmée par construction ; à vérifier à la main si une machine WSL2 est disponible.
435	6. **Espaces de noms PID et conteneurs.** `os.Getppid()` peut rendre 0 (parent hors de l'espace de noms) : règle du parent ignorée. DevDesk PID 1 dans un conteneur : raison `This is DevDesk itself`.
436	7. **Parent mort, sous-moissonneur.** Après la mort du parent, `getppid` rend PID 1 ou un sous-moissonneur (`systemd --user`, etc.), généralement né avant DevDesk : il sera grisé « This process started DevDesk ». Protection excessive, sans danger ; à documenter.
437	8. **Windows.** `os.Getppid` lit un instantané Toolhelp32 : le PID parent peut être celui d'un parent mort et repris ; la comparaison des heures règle ce cas. `CreateTime` du parent passe par `OpenProcess` : refusé (parent élevé) → protégé par prudence. PID 0 : `List` le vide déjà (`toSocket`), donc en pratique la ligne est grisée avec `reasonNoPID` ; la raison Windows ne s'affiche que pour une ligne `PID: "0"`, impossible aujourd'hui (voir Hypothèses).
438	9. **Coût par rendu.** `killable()` est appelé à chaque image de l'en-tête. Lecture d'heure seulement quand la ligne sélectionnée porte le PID du parent ; sous Windows, un `OpenProcess` par rendu sur cette ligne. Acceptable ; si une mesure le contredit, mémoriser le verdict par PID parent dans netdiag (pas dans ce lot).
439	10. **`testing` importé par du code de production.** Précédent : `internal/credentials/hoststore.go`. `testing.Testing()` est faux dans `dk`.
440	11. **Gardes existants.** `TestNothingHereRunsASubprocessOrTalksToDocker` ne lit que les fichiers non-test : l'`os/exec` du test d'intégration est permis. Le garde d'activité (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`) lit `ports_model.go` : pas de glyphe littéral, pas de nouveau fichier de vue à déclarer (`ports_commands.go` reste hors du garde).
441	12. **Irréversible.** Rien : aucun format de fichier, aucune configuration, aucune API externe ne change. Un revert rend le comportement actuel.
442	
443	## 8. Questions bloquantes
444	
445	**Q1 — `Yes` alors que la cible n'est plus dans le tableau rafraîchi.** Le critère 6 dit que la confirmation reste sur sa cible si le processus disparaît du tableau, et que `No`/`esc` la ferme sans signal ; il ne dit pas ce que fait `Yes` dans ce cas. Le critère 5 dit seulement que `Yes` agit sur le PID capturé.
446	- (a) Signaler quand même le PID capturé (lecture littérale du critère 5). Si le processus est sorti : `PID N is no longer running` sous Unix. Si son PID a été repris pendant que la modale était ouverte : le nouveau processus est tué. S-01b fermera ce cas.
447	- (b) **Recommandé** : avant le signal, vérifier que le dernier tableau reçu contient encore une ligne avec ce PID **et** le même nom ; sinon aucun signal, pied de page Warn `node (PID 4242) is no longer listed — not stopped`. Coût nul (aucune lecture système), ferme l'essentiel de la fenêtre du risque 4 jusqu'à S-01b. Si le processus a seulement fermé son socket, le port est libéré : refuser ne contrarie pas le but de l'utilisateur. Limites : tableau en pause ou périmé → on se fie aux dernières données ; même nom après reprise du PID → non détecté (c'est S-01b).
448	- (c) Fermer la confirmation automatiquement dès que la cible disparaît du tableau. Contredit le critère 6 (« la confirmation reste sur sa cible »).
449	
450	Le plan isole ce point dans `targetStillListed` (étape 3) ; avec (b), ajouter `TestYesOnAVanishedTargetSendsNothing` et `TestYesOnAPIDNowNamedDifferentlySendsNothing` (étape 3) et la ligne correspondante dans la matrice.
451	
452	## 9. Hypothèses (non bloquantes, option la plus prudente retenue)
453	
454	- Hypothèse : précédence self → PID 1 → Windows 0/4 → parent.
455	- Hypothèse : heures égales à la milliseconde, ou heure de DevDesk illisible → parent protégé.
456	- Hypothèse : `toSocket` continue de vider le PID 0 (sous Windows c'est un socket non attribué, `TIME_WAIT` surtout, pas le processus Idle) ; `killable()` grise quand même `Windows system process` pour une ligne `PID: "0"` si elle apparaissait, et `ports.Kill("0")` sous Windows nomme la raison. Le critère 3 est donc tenu pour PID 4 (System, qui tient 445 et 139) et en profondeur pour PID 0.
457	- Hypothèse : texte Windows sur deux paragraphes (`?\n\n`), comparé normalisé à la phrase du critère.
458	- Hypothèse : aide `K` sous Windows `End the selected process at once, after confirmation (Ports tab)`.
459	- Hypothèse : titre de modale `Kill Process` inchangé sur toutes les plateformes (Q6 non tranchée).
460	- Hypothèse : un nom de processus vide donne déjà `Send SIGKILL to  (PID N)?` aujourd'hui ; non corrigé ici (Linux inchangé, S-02a n°4), à signaler comme suivi.
461	- Hypothèse : le refus en profondeur (`ProtectedError`) s'affiche en Warn, pas en Error (Rule 128 : précondition non remplie).

1	package ports
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"os"
6		"runtime"
7		"sync/atomic"
8		"testing"
9	
10		gproc "github.com/shirou/gopsutil/v4/process"
11	)
12	
13	// What the package asks of the host about processes goes through these seams,
14	// so a test can substitute them (DEVDESK-708). They are written only by tests
15	// of this package, never while a Cmd runs.
16	var (
17		selfPID           = os.Getpid
18		parentPID         = os.Getppid
19		goos              = runtime.GOOS
20		procOS    osProcs = realOS{}
21	)
22	
23	// osProcs is everything this package asks the operating system about a single
24	// process: when it was created, and to end it.
25	type osProcs interface {
26		// createTime is the creation time in ms since the epoch. It is opaque: it
27		// is only compared with another value of the same function.
28		createTime(pid int) (int64, error)
29		// kill is SIGKILL, or TerminateProcess on Windows.
30		kill(pid int) error
31	}
32	
33	// realOS is the production osProcs.
34	type realOS struct{}
35	
36	func (realOS) createTime(pid int) (int64, error) {
37		p, err := gproc.NewProcess(int32(pid)) //nolint:gosec // a PID fits in int32 on every supported OS
38		if err != nil {
39			return 0, err
40		}
41		return p.CreateTime()
42	}
43	
44	// kill is the only place of this package that signals a process, and its first
45	// statement is the run-time guard (TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal).
46	func (realOS) kill(pid int) error {
47		refuseRealSignalUnderTest(pid)
48		p, err := os.FindProcess(pid)
49		if err != nil {
50			return fmt.Errorf("finding the process: %w", err)
51		}
52		return p.Kill()
53	}
54	
55	// realSignalsAllowed is flipped only by allowRealSignals(t) in the _test.go
56	// files of this package.
57	var realSignalsAllowed atomic.Bool
58	
59	// refuseRealSignalUnderTest panics in a test binary that did not allow real
60	// signals. It panics rather than returning an error: an error would be shown as
61	// an ordinary failed kill and the test could pass, leaving the guard silent.
62	func refuseRealSignalUnderTest(pid int) {
63		if testing.Testing() && !realSignalsAllowed.Load() {
64			panic(fmt.Sprintf("ports: a test reached a real signal to PID %d without a substituted procOS; "+
65				"replace procOS, or call allowRealSignals(t) for a child the test started "+
66				"(DEVDESK-708, docs/architecture/network.md)", pid))
67		}
68	}

1	package ports
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strconv"
6	)
7	
8	// Protection says why DevDesk refuses to signal a process, or that it does not
9	// (DEVDESK-708). The zero value is Unprotected, so a Protection nobody set
10	// never blocks anything.
11	type Protection int
12	
13	const (
14		// Unprotected is a process DevDesk may signal.
15		Unprotected Protection = iota
16		// ProtectedSelf is DevDesk's own process.
17		ProtectedSelf
18		// ProtectedInit is PID 1.
19		ProtectedInit
20		// ProtectedWindowsSystem is PID 0 or 4 on Windows (Idle and System).
21		ProtectedWindowsSystem
22		// ProtectedParent is the process that started DevDesk: the direct parent
23		// only, never a grandparent.
24		ProtectedParent
25	)
26	
27	// The sentences shown to the user for each refusal.
28	const (
29		ReasonSelf          = "This is DevDesk itself"
30		ReasonParent        = "This process started DevDesk"
31		ReasonInit          = "PID 1 is the system's init process"
32		ReasonWindowsSystem = "Windows system process"
33	)
34	
35	// Reason is the sentence to show for p, or "" for Unprotected.
36	func (p Protection) Reason() string {
37		switch p {
38		case ProtectedSelf:
39			return ReasonSelf
40		case ProtectedParent:
41			return ReasonParent
42		case ProtectedInit:
43			return ReasonInit
44		case ProtectedWindowsSystem:
45			return ReasonWindowsSystem
46		default:
47			return ""
48		}
49	}
50	
51	// hostView is what protectionFor needs to know about the host. parentBornFirst
52	// is a function so the creation time, which costs a system call, is read only
53	// when the PID asked about is the parent's.
54	type hostView struct {
55		self, parent    int
56		windows         bool
57		parentBornFirst func() bool
58	}
59	
60	// protectionFor is the rule, free of any system call. The order matters when
61	// one PID qualifies twice: DevDesk itself first, then PID 1 (also a parent
62	// inside a container), then the Windows system PIDs, then the parent. A parent
63	// PID of 0 means unknown (the parent lives outside this PID namespace) and
64	// never matches.
65	func protectionFor(pid int, h hostView) Protection {
66		switch {
67		case pid == h.self:
68			return ProtectedSelf
69		case pid == 1:
70			return ProtectedInit
71		case h.windows && (pid == 0 || pid == 4):
72			return ProtectedWindowsSystem
73		case h.parent > 0 && pid == h.parent && h.parentBornFirst():
74			return ProtectedParent
75		default:
76			return Unprotected
77		}
78	}
79	
80	// parentStartedFirst reports whether parent was created no later than self. A
81	// parent born after DevDesk is a process that reused the PID of the real one,
82	// which exited. Anything unreadable, and a tie, counts as true: when in doubt
83	// the parent is protected.
84	func parentStartedFirst(parent, self int) bool {
85		parentCreated, err := procOS.createTime(parent)
86		if err != nil {
87			return true
88		}
89		selfCreated, err := procOS.createTime(self)
90		if err != nil {
91			return true
92		}
93		return parentCreated <= selfCreated
94	}
95	
96	// protectionOf feeds protectionFor from the seams.
97	func protectionOf(n int) Protection {
98		self, parent := selfPID(), parentPID()
99		return protectionFor(n, hostView{
100			self:            self,
101			parent:          parent,
102			windows:         goos == "windows",
103			parentBornFirst: func() bool { return parentStartedFirst(parent, self) },
104		})
105	}
106	
107	// parsePID reads a PID in the one form DevDesk accepts: canonical decimal that
108	// fits in 32 bits. The kernel keeps only 32 bits (pid_t on Unix, a DWORD on
109	// Windows), so a wider number would reach a different process than the one
110	// checked: "4294967295" would become kill(-1), "4294967297" PID 1. Kill is the
111	// exported border, so it is checked here, once, for Kill and ProtectionOf.
112	// Signs, leading zeros and spaces are refused: the text must be what
113	// strconv.Itoa prints.
114	func parsePID(pid string) (int, bool) {
115		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(pid, 10, 32)
116		if err != nil || strconv.Itoa(int(n)) != pid {
117			return 0, false
118		}
119		return int(n), true
120	}
121	
122	// ProtectionOf says whether DevDesk refuses to signal the process pid. An
123	// empty, non-numeric, out-of-range or non-canonical pid is Unprotected: Kill
124	// refuses it as not a process id, so there is nothing to protect. It runs on
125	// every render, hence the lazy creation-time read.
126	func ProtectionOf(pid string) Protection {
127		n, ok := parsePID(pid)
128		if !ok {
129			return Unprotected
130		}
131		return protectionOf(n)
132	}
133	
134	// ProtectedError is the refusal Kill returns for a protected process. It is
135	// not an operating system error: it does not wrap os.ErrPermission.
136	type ProtectedError struct {
137		PID        int
138		Protection Protection
139	}
140	
141	func (e *ProtectedError) Error() string {
142		return fmt.Sprintf("PID %d not stopped: %s", e.PID, e.Protection.Reason())
143	}

1	// Package ports reads the machine's socket table, and ends a process holding
2	// one.
3	//
4	// It answers for **this machine**. That is the whole reason it exists: the
5	// Ports tab used to run `ss` inside `docker run --rm --net=host --pid=host
6	// --privileged`, and on Docker Desktop `--net=host` is the namespace of the
7	// Linux VM, not of the host. The tab therefore listed the VM's sockets — its
8	// NFS daemons, with two-digit PIDs — while not one of the host's listening
9	// sockets appeared, and `K` killed a process of the VM under the impression it
10	// was freeing a port on the machine (D55).
11	//
12	// The same sentence has been written at the top of `docker.runDiagHost` since
13	// §3.33 rapatriated DNS, ICMP, TCP, TLS and HTTP for exactly this reason.
14	// `RunSS` and `KillProcess` were the two that stayed behind.
15	//
16	// Nothing here starts a container, and nothing here needs Docker: the Ports tab
17	// now works on a machine that has none.
18	package ports
19	
20	import (
21		"context"
22		"fmt"
23		"net"
24		"strconv"
25	
26		gnet "github.com/shirou/gopsutil/v4/net"
27		gproc "github.com/shirou/gopsutil/v4/process"
28	)
29	
30	// Socket is one row of the table: a socket, and the process holding it.
31	//
32	// Every field is a string because every one of them is displayed, and the PID
33	// in particular is what the table is keyed on — an int would have to be
34	// formatted at each of the sites that compare it.
35	type Socket struct {
36		Protocol  string // tcp or udp, whichever family the address is on
37		State     string // LISTEN, ESTABLISHED, UNCONN, TIME_WAIT…
38		LocalAddr string
39		PeerAddr  string
40		PID       string // empty when no process could be attributed
41		Process   string
42	}
43	
44	// List returns the machine's TCP and UDP sockets.
45	//
46	// resolve asks for the addresses to be reported as host names where reverse DNS
47	// answers; see resolveAddrs for what that does and does not cover.
48	func List(ctx context.Context, resolve bool) ([]Socket, error) {
49		conns, err := gnet.ConnectionsWithContext(ctx, "inet")
50		if err != nil {
51			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading the socket table: %w", err)
52		}
53	
54		names := processNames(ctx)
55	
56		sockets := make([]Socket, 0, len(conns))
57		for _, c := range conns {
58			sockets = append(sockets, toSocket(c, names))
59		}
60	
61		if resolve {
62			resolveAddrs(ctx, sockets)
63		}
64		return sockets, nil
65	}
66	
67	// toSocket turns one connection into a row.
68	func toSocket(c gnet.ConnectionStat, names map[int32]string) Socket {
69		s := Socket{
70			Protocol:  protocolOf(c.Type),
71			State:     stateOf(c.Status, c.Type),
72			LocalAddr: formatAddr(c.Laddr, c.Family),
73			PeerAddr:  formatAddr(c.Raddr, c.Family),
74		}
75		// A PID of zero is not a process: it is the system declining to attribute
76		// the socket to one, and `K` keys on this field. Left as "0" it would give
77		// the row something that looks killable, and Kill would then be asked to
78		// signal a process id that means "every process in the group" on Unix.
79		if c.Pid > 0 {
80			s.PID = strconv.FormatInt(int64(c.Pid), 10)
81			s.Process = names[c.Pid]
82		}
83		return s
84	}
85	
86	// Kill sends SIGKILL — TerminateProcess on Windows — to the process holding a
87	// socket.
88	//
89	// It replaces `docker run --pid=host --privileged <image> kill -9 <pid>`, which
90	// on Docker Desktop signalled a process of the VM (D55). The consequence worth
91	// knowing is that DevDesk now signals with the rights it actually has: another
92	// user's process, or a service, comes back as a refusal from the operating
93	// system rather than as a success against the wrong machine.
94	//
95	// The signal leaves through procOS.kill, the single point of the package that
96	// sends one; in a test binary it panics unless the test substituted procOS
97	// (DEVDESK-708).
98	//
99	// DevDesk itself, its direct parent, PID 1 and, on Windows, PIDs 0 and 4 are
100	// refused with a *ProtectedError before anything is sent. A pid outside int32
101	// or not in canonical form is refused first, as "not a process id" (parsePID).
102	// The protection check comes
103	// before the n <= 0 one because PID 0 is a protected process on Windows.
104	func Kill(pid string) error {
105		n, ok := parsePID(pid)
106		if !ok {
107			return fmt.Errorf("not a process id: %q", pid)
108		}
109		if p := protectionOf(n); p != Unprotected {
110			return &ProtectedError{PID: n, Protection: p}
111		}
112		if n <= 0 {
113			return fmt.Errorf("not a process id: %q", pid)
114		}
115		if err := procOS.kill(n); err != nil {
116			return fmt.Errorf("killing process %s: %w", pid, err)
117		}
118		return nil
119	}
120	
121	// processNames maps PID to process name, from **one** enumeration.
122	//
123	// The obvious implementation — process.NewProcess(pid).Name() per socket — is
124	// the one that does not work. On Windows that path goes through OpenProcess and
125	// QueryFullProcessImageName, which needs rights over the target: measured on
126	// this machine, 98 of 189 sockets came back "Access denied", and the Process
127	// column would have been empty for every service on the box. Processes() reads
128	// a Toolhelp32 snapshot instead and named all 294 processes in 11 ms, elevated
129	// or not.
130	//
131	// So the bulk enumeration is not an optimisation over the per-PID call. It is
132	// the difference between a column that is filled in and one that is not.
133	//
134	// A failure here is not a failure of the listing: a table of sockets with no
135	// process names still says which ports are open, and that is most of what it is
136	// read for.
137	func processNames(ctx context.Context) map[int32]string {
138		procs, err := gproc.ProcessesWithContext(ctx)
139		if err != nil {
140			return nil
141		}
142		names := make(map[int32]string, len(procs))
143		for _, p := range procs {
144			if name, err := p.NameWithContext(ctx); err == nil && name != "" {
145				names[p.Pid] = name
146			}
147		}
148		return names
149	}
150	
151	// protocolOf reports tcp or udp. Both families print the same word, as `ss`
152	// does: the address beside it already says which one it is on.
153	func protocolOf(sockType uint32) string {
154		switch sockType {
155		case 1: // SOCK_STREAM
156			return "tcp"
157		case 2: // SOCK_DGRAM
158			return "udp"
159		default:
160			return ""
161		}
162	}
163	
164	// stateOf normalises the state, and neither substitution is cosmetic.
165	//
166	// An unconnected UDP socket is reported as "NONE" on Linux and as nothing at all
167	// on Windows, so the same socket read differently depending on where DevDesk was
168	// running. UNCONN is what the table showed when `ss` produced it, and it is what
169	// the socket is.
170	//
171	// ESTABLISHED is shortened to ESTAB for the reason `ss` shortens it: the State
172	// column is ten cells wide, so the long spelling is truncated to "ESTABLISHE" —
173	// and the filter token the user toggles with `e` reads better short.
174	func stateOf(status string, sockType uint32) string {
175		if sockType == 2 && (status == "" || status == "NONE") {
176			return "UNCONN"
177		}
178		if status == "ESTABLISHED" {
179			return "ESTAB"
180		}
181		return status
182	}
183	
184	// formatAddr renders an endpoint the way the table has always shown one:
185	// host:port, bracketed for IPv6, and the wildcard form for the peer of a socket
186	// that has none.
187	func formatAddr(a gnet.Addr, family uint32) string {
188		if a.IP == "" && a.Port == 0 {
189			if isIPv6(family) {
190				return "[::]:*"
191			}
192			return "0.0.0.0:*"
193		}
194		return net.JoinHostPort(a.IP, strconv.FormatUint(uint64(a.Port), 10))
195	}
196	
197	// isIPv6 reports whether the address family is AF_INET6. The constant differs
198	// between platforms — 23 on Windows, 10 on Linux, 30 on Darwin — and gopsutil
199	// passes through whichever the kernel used, so all three are named here rather
200	// than compared against one.
201	func isIPv6(family uint32) bool {
202		return family == 23 || family == 10 || family == 30
203	}

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

# TUI — Bubble Tea behavior & architecture

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

- Format: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg`
- Examples: `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`, `ConfirmModalYesMsg`
- Always document with a comment
- Group related messages together in the file

### Rule 110 : NEVER modify the model inside a Cmd ⚠️

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |

```go
// ❌ WRONG — race condition
func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    return func() tea.Msg {
        m.authenticated = false  // DANGER
        return nil
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT — message + Update()
type LogoutCompleteMsg struct{}

func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    url := m.urlInput.Value()  // copy the data we need
    return func() tea.Msg {
        auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
        _ = auth.Logout(url)
        return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
    }
}

case LogoutCompleteMsg:
    m.authenticated = false  // thread-safe inside Update()
    m.user = nil
    return m, nil
```

**Golden rule**: Cmds do the "dirty work" (I/O), then send a message to `Update()`.

### Rule 126 : Scan cache behavior (Images & Workspaces)

| Action | Disk cache | Memory cache | Scan triggered |
|--------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| `Enter` (scanned item) | Read | Read | No |
| `Enter` (not scanned) | — | — | No |
| `ctrl+s` (in progress) | Blocked | Blocked | No |
| `ctrl+s` (available) | Overwritten | Updated | Yes (item only) |
| `A` (unscanned) | Unchanged | Unchanged | Yes (unscanned) |
| `ctrl+a` (all) | **Purged** | **Purged** | Yes (all) |

**`ctrl+a` must clear the cache before relaunching the scans:**
```go
// ✅ CORRECT
func (m Model) requestScanAll() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    var keys []string
    for _, img := range m.images {
        delete(m.scanCache, name)  // in-memory purge inside Update()
        keys = append(keys, name)
    }
    return m, tea.Batch(deleteScanCacheCmd(keys), batchScanCmd(keys, m.defaultScanOpts()))
}
```

### Rule 128 : Footer messages — three levels, centered, one component

**`components.FooterMessage` is the only implementation.** A view does not
render its own message: it declares one, sets it from `Update()`, and
renders it via `m.footer.View(width, status)`.

There used to be eight of them, one per view, each with its own fields,
timer, and lipgloss block. That is what produced the flaw this component
removes: nobody ever centered the error branch, in any of the eight, so
errors were left-aligned everywhere while notices were centered.

#### The three levels

They are defined by **what happened**, not by how it feels:

| Level | Meaning | Color |
|--------|------|---------|
| `Error` | an operation failed, or the system refused it | `ColorFooterError` = the red of **CRITICAL** CVEs |
| `Warn` | the action cannot be honored as requested, but nothing failed: an unmet precondition, already in progress, not applicable here | `ColorFooterWarn` = the orange of **MEDIUM** CVEs |
| `Info` | a neutral fact, or a successful operation | `ColorFooterInfo` = `ColorText`, the ordinary text color |

Info is not bold, the other two are: the hierarchy runs through weight as
much as through hue, and a neutral info in bold would turn back into an
alert.

The colors are **semantic aliases** assigned in `ApplyTheme` (`colors.go`),
like the viewer's syntax colors: no theme file gains a key. They target the
**severity** names rather than `ColorError` / `ColorWarn` — the default
theme makes them coincide, so the choice is invisible today; it stops being
invisible in a theme that separates them.

#### What is forbidden

- ❌ `theme.StatusErrorStyle`, `StatusOKStyle`, `StatusWarningStyle`, or
  `ColorHighlight` inside a `RenderFooter`, a `renderInfoLine`, or a
  `renderInfoText` — `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage` scans the sources
  and fails, naming the file, line, and function.
- ❌ **Green** in a footer. It is reserved for status icons (Rule 121).
- ❌ A **left-aligned** message. `View` centers, always, across the full
  width.
- ❌ A local timer (`clearFooterCmd`, `clearInfoMsgCmd`, …): the component
  carries it.

#### Mandatory pattern

```go
// 1. The model declares a field.
type Model struct {
    footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
}

// 2. Update() sets the message and returns its timer. A message set without
//    its timer never disappears.
case SomeErrorMsg:
    log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", msg.Err)
    return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to load data — check logs")

case ScanAlreadyRunningMsg:
    return m, m.footer.Warn("Scan already in progress")

// 3. Update() offers unhandled messages to the component, which consumes
//    the expiry addressed to it.
m.footer.Handle(msg)
return m, nil

// 4. RenderFooter() renders the line, blank included — Rule 124 budgets it.
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "
" + m.footer.View(width, m.status())
}
```

**The expiry carries an id** (`ClearFooterMsg{ID}`): a stale timer does not
clear the message that took its predecessor's place. That is what makes the
type shareable across packages, and it fixes, in passing, a flaw all eight
implementations shared — a message set at t+2.9s was cleared at t+3s by the
previous one's timer.

#### `Status` — what has no timer

A progress indicator, a hint, a loading state: these are **states**, not
events. They are derived on every frame and passed as `View`'s second
argument, never set as a message — a line set when the first repo starts
would be cleared while the tenth is still running.

```go
func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
    if m.loading && len(m.table.Items()) == 0 {
        // the view's own load: the shared dot, with WantsBlink
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: "Loading images...", Activity: true}
    }
    // work the router tracks (a run in the registry): the shared dot
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.progressLine(), Activity: m.anyRunning()}
}
```

Precedence in `View`: **error → warning → info → status**. A failure the
user has not read takes priority over the progress of whatever is still
running.

One field prefixes the line with a mark:

| Field | Mark | Use it for | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Activity: true` | the shared activity dot, `●` / `○` (same glyph and colour as the row dots, `indicator.Running`) | any loading or running state: work the **router tracks** (a run in the jobs registry) and a view's own load (`WantsBlink()`) | the router's 500 ms blink phase: the view calls `m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` from its `jobs.FrameMsg` handler |

The braille spinner is removed (DEVDESK-377): `Status.Spinner`,
`FooterMessage.SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` and
`theme.SpinnerStyle` no longer exist, and no file under `internal/` may import
`charm.land/bubbles/v2/spinner`. `TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner` and
`TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone` (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`)
fail on a reintroduction, with no exception. `dk setup` has no router: it shows
a fixed `●` and the pending text, with no blink. Without a `SetBlinkPhase`
call the dot is steady on. `●` and `○` are one column wide and share a width,
so the phase never shifts the text.

A future `Activity` value that does not depend on the jobs registry must make
its view implement `WantsBlink() bool` (return `status().Activity`, as the
forge explorer does); otherwise the router arms no animation chain and the dot
stays fixed on `●`.

#### A table's loading state belongs to the footer

**When a `datatable` is loading, the table stays on screen** and the
loading state is an info message with a mark (the shared activity dot, for the
view's own load as well as for work the router tracks), in the footer only. A body that replaces itself with a loading screen loses its header and columns for the
duration of every `ctrl+r`, then regains them: a layout jump on every
refresh.

**A footer mark is for a table's data loading, never for one row.**
What is happening to a single row (a scan, a clone, a stop) is that row's
activity dot (Rule 125, "The activity column"); when the selected row has a
footer detail with a glyph (`Detail.Glyph`), the footer shows no dot: the
row's own dot already moves.

Mandatory consequence: the empty message ("No images found") is
**conditioned on loading being finished**, otherwise the table announces the
absence of what it is still looking for.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
loading body in the table views it covers. There is no declared exception.

#### Tests — the timer really does sleep

`tea.Tick` blocks for its entire duration, and `testutil.Msgs` runs the
whole batch it is given: a test that inspects a `Cmd` carrying the timer
pays the full three seconds. The timer starts when the `Cmd` is **built**
(`PostFooter` and `FooterMessage.set` call `tea.Tick` at that moment), not
when it runs: shortening the duration after the `Update` that returned the
`Cmd` is too late, the three seconds are already armed.

- To verify that a message **disappears**, build the expiry rather than
  running the `Cmd`:
  `feed(t, m, components.ClearFooterMsg{ID: m.footer.ID()})`.
- For a test that must drain the `Cmd` (because it is looking for another
  one inside it), shorten the timer **before the `Update` that builds the
  `Cmd`**, as the first line of the test:
  `testutil.FastTimers(t, &components.FooterMsgDuration)`. A helper that
  drains a `Cmd` (like `drive` in `internal/app`) only covers the `Cmds` it
  builds itself.
- `requireNoRealFooterWait(t)` (`internal/app/footer_timer_guard_test.go`)
  fails a test that took over 1.5 s: use it in a test that builds and drains
  footer `Cmds`.

`FooterMsgDuration` is an exported `var` for this reason alone; its
production value is fixed by `TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds`.

#### Other prohibitions

Mandatory log format: `log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", err)`

- ❌ `err.Error()` directly in the UI (except a validation message already
  written to be read)
- ❌ Replacing the view with an error screen (except fatal initialization
  errors)
- ❌ Ignoring an error without `log.Printf`

# TUI — Bubble Tea behavior & architecture

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

- Format: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg`
- Examples: `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`, `ConfirmModalYesMsg`
- Always document with a comment
- Group related messages together in the file

### Rule 110 : NEVER modify the model inside a Cmd ⚠️

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |

```go
// ❌ WRONG — race condition
func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    return func() tea.Msg {
        m.authenticated = false  // DANGER
        return nil
    }
}

// ✅ CORRECT — message + Update()
type LogoutCompleteMsg struct{}

func (m *Model) logout() tea.Cmd {
    url := m.urlInput.Value()  // copy the data we need
    return func() tea.Msg {
        auth := gitlabpkg.NewAuth(m.storage)
        _ = auth.Logout(url)
        return LogoutCompleteMsg{}
    }
}

case LogoutCompleteMsg:
    m.authenticated = false  // thread-safe inside Update()
    m.user = nil
    return m, nil
```

**Golden rule**: Cmds do the "dirty work" (I/O), then send a message to `Update()`.

### Rule 126 : Scan cache behavior (Images & Workspaces)

| Action | Disk cache | Memory cache | Scan triggered |
|--------|-------------|---------------|------------|
| `Enter` (scanned item) | Read | Read | No |
| `Enter` (not scanned) | — | — | No |
| `ctrl+s` (in progress) | Blocked | Blocked | No |
| `ctrl+s` (available) | Overwritten | Updated | Yes (item only) |
| `A` (unscanned) | Unchanged | Unchanged | Yes (unscanned) |
| `ctrl+a` (all) | **Purged** | **Purged** | Yes (all) |

**`ctrl+a` must clear the cache before relaunching the scans:**
```go
// ✅ CORRECT
func (m Model) requestScanAll() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    var keys []string
    for _, img := range m.images {
        delete(m.scanCache, name)  // in-memory purge inside Update()
        keys = append(keys, name)
    }
    return m, tea.Batch(deleteScanCacheCmd(keys), batchScanCmd(keys, m.defaultScanOpts()))
}
```

### Rule 128 : Footer messages — three levels, centered, one component

**`components.FooterMessage` is the only implementation.** A view does not
render its own message: it declares one, sets it from `Update()`, and
renders it via `m.footer.View(width, status)`.

There used to be eight of them, one per view, each with its own fields,
timer, and lipgloss block. That is what produced the flaw this component
removes: nobody ever centered the error branch, in any of the eight, so
errors were left-aligned everywhere while notices were centered.

#### The three levels

They are defined by **what happened**, not by how it feels:

| Level | Meaning | Color |
|--------|------|---------|
| `Error` | an operation failed, or the system refused it | `ColorFooterError` = the red of **CRITICAL** CVEs |
| `Warn` | the action cannot be honored as requested, but nothing failed: an unmet precondition, already in progress, not applicable here | `ColorFooterWarn` = the orange of **MEDIUM** CVEs |
| `Info` | a neutral fact, or a successful operation | `ColorFooterInfo` = `ColorText`, the ordinary text color |

Info is not bold, the other two are: the hierarchy runs through weight as
much as through hue, and a neutral info in bold would turn back into an
alert.

The colors are **semantic aliases** assigned in `ApplyTheme` (`colors.go`),
like the viewer's syntax colors: no theme file gains a key. They target the
**severity** names rather than `ColorError` / `ColorWarn` — the default
theme makes them coincide, so the choice is invisible today; it stops being
invisible in a theme that separates them.

#### What is forbidden

- ❌ `theme.StatusErrorStyle`, `StatusOKStyle`, `StatusWarningStyle`, or
  `ColorHighlight` inside a `RenderFooter`, a `renderInfoLine`, or a
  `renderInfoText` — `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage` scans the sources
  and fails, naming the file, line, and function.
- ❌ **Green** in a footer. It is reserved for status icons (Rule 121).
- ❌ A **left-aligned** message. `View` centers, always, across the full
  width.
- ❌ A local timer (`clearFooterCmd`, `clearInfoMsgCmd`, …): the component
  carries it.

#### Mandatory pattern

```go
// 1. The model declares a field.
type Model struct {
    footer sharedcomponents.FooterMessage
}

// 2. Update() sets the message and returns its timer. A message set without
//    its timer never disappears.
case SomeErrorMsg:
    log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", msg.Err)
    return m, m.footer.Error("Failed to load data — check logs")

case ScanAlreadyRunningMsg:
    return m, m.footer.Warn("Scan already in progress")

// 3. Update() offers unhandled messages to the component, which consumes
//    the expiry addressed to it.
m.footer.Handle(msg)
return m, nil

// 4. RenderFooter() renders the line, blank included — Rule 124 budgets it.
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    return theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "
" + m.footer.View(width, m.status())
}
```

**The expiry carries an id** (`ClearFooterMsg{ID}`): a stale timer does not
clear the message that took its predecessor's place. That is what makes the
type shareable across packages, and it fixes, in passing, a flaw all eight
implementations shared — a message set at t+2.9s was cleared at t+3s by the
previous one's timer.

#### `Status` — what has no timer

A progress indicator, a hint, a loading state: these are **states**, not
events. They are derived on every frame and passed as `View`'s second
argument, never set as a message — a line set when the first repo starts
would be cleared while the tenth is still running.

```go
func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
    if m.loading && len(m.table.Items()) == 0 {
        // the view's own load: the shared dot, with WantsBlink
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: "Loading images...", Activity: true}
    }
    // work the router tracks (a run in the registry): the shared dot
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.progressLine(), Activity: m.anyRunning()}
}
```

Precedence in `View`: **error → warning → info → status**. A failure the
user has not read takes priority over the progress of whatever is still
running.

One field prefixes the line with a mark:

| Field | Mark | Use it for | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Activity: true` | the shared activity dot, `●` / `○` (same glyph and colour as the row dots, `indicator.Running`) | any loading or running state: work the **router tracks** (a run in the jobs registry) and a view's own load (`WantsBlink()`) | the router's 500 ms blink phase: the view calls `m.footer.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink)` from its `jobs.FrameMsg` handler |

The braille spinner is removed (DEVDESK-377): `Status.Spinner`,
`FooterMessage.SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` and
`theme.SpinnerStyle` no longer exist, and no file under `internal/` may import
`charm.land/bubbles/v2/spinner`. `TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner` and
`TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone` (`internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`)
fail on a reintroduction, with no exception. `dk setup` has no router: it shows
a fixed `●` and the pending text, with no blink. Without a `SetBlinkPhase`
call the dot is steady on. `●` and `○` are one column wide and share a width,
so the phase never shifts the text.

A future `Activity` value that does not depend on the jobs registry must make
its view implement `WantsBlink() bool` (return `status().Activity`, as the
forge explorer does); otherwise the router arms no animation chain and the dot
stays fixed on `●`.

#### A table's loading state belongs to the footer

**When a `datatable` is loading, the table stays on screen** and the
loading state is an info message with a mark (the shared activity dot, for the
view's own load as well as for work the router tracks), in the footer only. A body that replaces itself with a loading screen loses its header and columns for the
duration of every `ctrl+r`, then regains them: a layout jump on every
refresh.

**A footer mark is for a table's data loading, never for one row.**
What is happening to a single row (a scan, a clone, a stop) is that row's
activity dot (Rule 125, "The activity column"); when the selected row has a
footer detail with a glyph (`Detail.Glyph`), the footer shows no dot: the
row's own dot already moves.

Mandatory consequence: the empty message ("No images found") is
**conditioned on loading being finished**, otherwise the table announces the
absence of what it is still looking for.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
loading body in the table views it covers. There is no declared exception.

#### Tests — the timer really does sleep

`tea.Tick` blocks for its entire duration, and `testutil.Msgs` runs the
whole batch it is given: a test that inspects a `Cmd` carrying the timer
pays the full three seconds. The timer starts when the `Cmd` is **built**
(`PostFooter` and `FooterMessage.set` call `tea.Tick` at that moment), not
when it runs: shortening the duration after the `Update` that returned the
`Cmd` is too late, the three seconds are already armed.

- To verify that a message **disappears**, build the expiry rather than
  running the `Cmd`:
  `feed(t, m, components.ClearFooterMsg{ID: m.footer.ID()})`.
- For a test that must drain the `Cmd` (because it is looking for another
  one inside it), shorten the timer **before the `Update` that builds the
  `Cmd`**, as the first line of the test:
  `testutil.FastTimers(t, &components.FooterMsgDuration)`. A helper that
  drains a `Cmd` (like `drive` in `internal/app`) only covers the `Cmds` it
  builds itself.
- `requireNoRealFooterWait(t)` (`internal/app/footer_timer_guard_test.go`)
  fails a test that took over 1.5 s: use it in a test that builds and drains
  footer `Cmds`.

`FooterMsgDuration` is an exported `var` for this reason alone; its
production value is fixed by `TestAMessageGetsThreeSeconds`.

#### Other prohibitions

Mandatory log format: `log.Printf("ERROR [package/view] action: %v", err)`

- ❌ `err.Error()` directly in the UI (except a validation message already
  written to be read)
- ❌ Replacing the view with an error screen (except fatal initialization
  errors)
- ❌ Ignoring an error without `log.Printf`
